risks.note: Management names 'intense price competition' among the major risks it has identified. The MD&A adds that while volume growth stayed strong, 'the value growth in the industry has seen a slow-down due to an intense competitive environment fuelled by new entrants as well as some of the legacy players fighting for market share', and that competitive intensity is driving a sharp structural shift towards hard luggage AT VALUE PRICING - i.e. mix is moving toward a category the Company must serve at lower realisations, which is precisely why the premiumisation and in-house premium manufacturing push is being funded.
risks.risk: Intense price competition and value-growth compression in the luggage industry

risks.note: Listed by management as a major identified risk. The MD&A opens by noting several geo-political disruptions globally that directly impacted the global economy and particularly the travel industry, and the Outlook section concedes 'several uncertainties due to larger geo-political factors' even while the Company has grown ahead of the market. Management states future growth prospects and cash flow generation could be materially impacted by these risks.
risks.risk: Cost risk from global geo-political upheaval

risks.note: Explicitly named by management as a major risk. The Company imports inputs and finished backpacks, and continues to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China, so rupee depreciation feeds directly into landed cost in a category where value pricing limits the ability to pass it through.

The Company states it has diversified Backpack supplies by building a larger supplier base within India 'while continuing to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China', explicitly to de-risk against potential geo-political and macro-economic uncertainties - the mitigation itself confirms residual cross-border sourcing exposure in a category management calls a strong growth driver. The BRSR material-issues table separately flags Sustainable Supply Chain as a risk with negative financial implications, since gaps at supplier locations may lead to operational disruption, reputational exposure and regulatory concerns.
risks.risk: Supplier and sourcing concentration in the Backpack category (Bangladesh and China)

risks.note: Growth depends on domestic travel and marriage/wedding demand. Geo-political headwinds have already caused a loss of demand for international travel, and the shift towards domestic destinations 'has impacted the size mix away from larger sized luggage to medium sized luggage and cabin size' - smaller units at lower price points. Management's own instruction for the year ahead is to stay focussed on specific channels, categories and consumer segments expected to drive market growth.
risks.risk: Demand is discretionary and travel-linked, with an adverse size-mix shift

risks.note: The BRSR grievance table shows customer complaints filed rose to 1,51,444 in FY 2025-26 from 97,382 in FY 2024-25, with 1,395 pending at year end which the Company says 'will be attended/resolved during FY 2026-27' (the prior year's pending complaints had been resolved). In a brand-led category where consumers are said to prioritise warranties and quality, a step-up of this size is a warranty-cost and brand-equity watch item.

The BRSR material-issues table classifies Climate Strategy & Emission Management as a RISK with negative financial implications: physical impacts such as extreme weather affect operations, logistics and supply chains, while transition factors including regulation and market expectations can affect long-term performance. Against this, the Company's own disclosed trajectory has moved the wrong way - Scope 1 and 2 emissions rose 26% and energy intensity rose 11% versus the FY 2024 baseline, driven by the scaled-up Jaipur plant, against FY 2028 targets of 25% and 20% REDUCTIONS respectively.
risks.risk: Climate transition and physical risk to operations, logistics and supply chains

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table classifies Occupational Health & Safety as a RISK with negative financial implications: workplace incidents may lead to injuries, disruption and financial exposure, with direct implications for regulatory compliance and continuity of operations. Exposure is structurally elevated because the great majority of the workforce is 'other than permanent' - 2,200 of 2,223 workers and 2,956 of 4,012 employees - across injection-moulding and automated manufacturing operations.

currentContext.expansion: Driven by continued growth in the hard luggage category, the Company along with its wholly owned subsidiary Safari Manufacturing Limited has further scaled up capacity at its manufacturing plants for polypropylene and polycarbonate zippered hard luggage in Jaipur, Rajasthan and Halol, Gujarat, through investments in additional machinery and a focus on increased efficiencies via automation. During the year under review the Company started indigenising its premium portfolio, building in-house production capabilities to produce high-quality, well-crafted premium hard luggage - an investment management explicitly links to improving profitability as it scales up in higher price segments. On the front end, the Company has continued to expand its footprint of exclusive retail stores in premium high-footfall areas, with exclusive retail plus Premium Large Format stores positioned as the key drivers of the premiumisation agenda; a licensed super-premium brand, Carlton, is to be launched in FY 2026-27. Back-end investment continues in automation and technology for more efficient manufacturing and a responsive supply chain, including modern technology in ERP, warehousing and planning capability, plus specialised supply-chain and front-end capability for the quick-commerce channel. Backpack supply has been diversified by building a larger supplier base within India while retaining key vendors in Bangladesh and China. On energy infrastructure, a 4.25 MW rooftop solar system was installed (3 MW at SML's Jaipur Plant and 1.25 MW at SML's Halol Plant); SML's Jaipur plant itself was commissioned in the last quarter of FY 2024-25 and scaled operations in FY 2025-26. No rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative, and the named disclosures supplied carry no usable figure.

capex_expansion.body: Driven by continued growth in the hard luggage category, the Company along with its wholly owned subsidiary Safari Manufacturing Limited has further scaled up capacity at its manufacturing plants for polypropylene and polycarbonate zippered hard luggage in Jaipur, Rajasthan and Halol, Gujarat, through investments in additional machinery and a focus on increased efficiencies via automation. During the year under review the Company started indigenising its premium portfolio, building in-house production capabilities to produce high-quality, well-crafted premium hard luggage - an investment …

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Brand leadership: recognised as the 'No. 1 Luggage Brand in India' in revenue terms for the third successive year (Euromonitor International; Personal Accessories 2026 ed; Luggage category; all retail channels, value RSP terms; 2025 data)

- Backward-integrated manufacturing: in-house hard-luggage production in PP and PC …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management names 'intense price competition' among the major risks it has identified. The MD&A adds that while volume growth stayed strong, 'the value growth in the industry has seen a slow-down due to an intense competitive environment fuelled by new entrants as well as some of the legacy players fighting for market share', and that competitive intensity is driving a sharp structural shift towards hard luggage AT VALUE PRICING - i.e. mix is moving toward a category the Company must serve at lower realisations, which is precisely why the premiumisation and in-house premium manufacturing push is being funded.
- Listed by management as a major identified risk. The MD&A opens by noting several geo-political disruptions globally that directly impacted the global economy and particularly the travel industry, and the Outlook section concedes 'several uncertainties due to larger geo-political factors' even while the Company has grown ahead of the market. Management states future growth prospects and cash flow generation could be materially impacted by these risks.
- Explicitly named by management as a major risk. The Company imports inputs and finished backpacks, and continues to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China, so rupee depreciation feeds directly into landed cost in a category where value pricing limits the ability to pass it through.
- The Company states it has diversified Backpack supplies by building a larger supplier base within India 'while continuing to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China', explicitly to de-risk against potential geo-political and macro-economic uncertainties - the mitigation itself confirms residual cross-border sourcing exposure in a category management calls a strong growth driver. The BRSR material-issues table separately flags Sustainable Supply Chain as a risk with negative financial implications, since gaps at supplier locations may lead to operational disruption, reputational exposure and regulatory concerns.
- Growth depends on domestic travel and marriage/wedding demand. Geo-political headwinds have already caused a loss of demand for international travel, and the shift towards domestic destinations 'has impacted the size mix away from larger sized luggage to medium sized luggage and cabin size' - smaller units at lower price points. Management's own instruction for the year ahead is to stay focussed on specific channels, categories and consumer segments expected to drive market growth.
- The BRSR grievance table shows customer complaints filed rose to 1,51,444 in FY 2025-26 from 97,382 in FY 2024-25, with 1,395 pending at year end which the Company says 'will be attended/resolved during FY 2026-27' (the prior year's pending complaints had been resolved). In a brand-led category where consumers are said to prioritise warranties and quality, a step-up of this size is a warranty-cost and brand-equity watch item.
- The BRSR material-issues table classifies Climate Strategy & Emission Management as a RISK with negative financial implications: physical impacts such as extreme weather affect operations, logistics and supply chains, while transition factors including regulation and market expectations can affect long-term performance. Against this, the Company's own disclosed trajectory has moved the wrong way - Scope 1 and 2 emissions rose 26% and energy intensity rose 11% versus the FY 2024 baseline, driven by the scaled-up Jaipur plant, against FY 2028 targets of 25% and 20% REDUCTIONS respectively.
- The BRSR material-issues table classifies Occupational Health & Safety as a RISK with negative financial implications: workplace incidents may lead to injuries, disruption and financial exposure, with direct implications for regulatory compliance and continuity of operations. Exposure is structurally elevated because the great majority of the workforce is 'other than permanent' - 2,200 of 2,223 workers and 2,956 of 4,012 employees - across injection-moulding and automated manufacturing operations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Premiumisation through a lifestyle-segmented, multi-brand roster: Urban Jungle (a casual premium brand focussing on the youth, run with a digital-first approach), Safari Select (a semi-formal design approach positioned as a premium upgrade for Safari brand loyalists) and Carlton, taken as a long-term brand licence to foray into the super-premium price segment, to be launched in FY 2026-27
- Aggressive investment in building share in the mid and premium price-segments to improve price realisation through product-mix improvement, described as critical for long-term sustainable growth and …

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

hero.oneLiner: Safari Industries (India) Limited, established in 1980 and based in Mumbai, designs, manufactures, trades and markets luggage, backpacks and travel accessories, and has been recognised as the 'No. 1 Luggage Brand in India' in revenue terms for the third successive year (Euromonitor International).
